Comprehensive analysis of charging station operations, demand patterns, grid load dynamics, and optimization opportunities
Dataset: 8,354 sessions across 20+ stations • Generated: May 07, 2026 • Audience: Infrastructure Managers & Grid Planners
ⓘ Data note: The dataset contains only Urban and Highway location types (no Suburban records) and only Off-Peak and Peak time slots (no Mid-Peak records). Charts that include Suburban or Mid-Peak categories show zero values where data is absent.

Executive Summary — Top 5 Findings

  1. Average waiting time is 9.5 min across the network; Highway locations during Peak periods experience the longest waits.
  2. Mean station load reaches its highest levels during Peak hours, with Highway stations averaging 84.0 kW.
  3. Renewable energy ratio averages 35.4%, peaking during Clear weather conditions but dropping significantly under Cloudy and Rainy conditions.
  4. Electricity price and renewable ratio show a correlation of r=-0.005, suggesting limited price-signal alignment with green energy availability.
  5. Mean optimization reward is -11.83, with Highway locations during Off-Peak showing the most favorable optimization conditions.

2. Queue Length & Waiting Time Analysis

Examine queue lengths and waiting times by station, time slot, vehicle type, and traffic density to identify bottleneck patterns and quantify the customer experience impact.

Wait Time Heatmap: Time Slot × Location

Figure 2.1: Heatmap of average waiting time (minutes) across time slots and location types. Darker cells indicate worse customer experience.

Waiting Time Distribution

Top 10 Stations by Wait Time

Key Takeaways

▸Off-Peak locations during Highway slots experience the longest waiting times, driven by high traffic density and queue buildup.
▸P90 waiting time reaches 16.0 minutes, meaning 10% of customers wait longer than this threshold.
▸Queue length and waiting time are strongly correlated (r=-0.005), confirming that queue management directly impacts customer experience.
Critical Finding: The correlation between queue length and waiting time is r=-0.01. With P90 wait times reaching 16.0 minutes, queue management at high-traffic Highway stations during Peak hours should be the top operational priority.

Assess energy consumption patterns, station load profiles across time slots and days of the week, and the relationship between charging power levels and grid stress.

4. Renewable Energy Integration & Dynamic Pricing

Evaluate the renewable energy ratio across different conditions and analyze how dynamic electricity pricing correlates with demand, renewable availability, and optimization rewards.

Renewable Ratio by Weather Condition

Figure 4.1: Average renewable energy ratio by weather condition. Clear weather enables significantly higher renewable penetration.
Figure 4.2: Renewable energy ratio by time slot. Off-Peak periods benefit from marginally higher renewable availability.

Renewable Ratio: Weather × Time Slot

Figure 4.3: Renewable energy ratio across weather conditions and time slots, highlighting the best windows for green charging.

Price Dynamics

Figure 4.4: Average electricity price by time slot. Peak pricing is elevated but the spread across slots is narrower than expected for optimal load shifting.
Figure 4.5: Scatter plot of electricity price vs. renewable energy ratio. The weak correlation (r=-0.005) suggests pricing is not well-aligned with renewable availability.

Key Takeaways

▸Renewable ratio is highest during Clear weather (35.7%), making these periods ideal for incentivizing charging.
▸The correlation between electricity price and renewable ratio is weak (r=-0.005), indicating a missed opportunity for price-driven green charging.
▸Off-Peak periods show marginally higher renewable ratios (39.3%), supporting off-peak charging as a sustainability lever.
Opportunity: The weak correlation (r=-0.005) between electricity price and renewable ratio indicates that current pricing does not effectively incentivize green charging. Introducing renewable-responsive pricing could shift demand toward high-renewable windows, improving both sustainability scores and grid optimization rewards (current correlation between renewable ratio and optimization reward: r=0.590).

6. Optimization Insights & Recommendations

Synthesize findings into actionable recommendations for load balancing, queue management, pricing strategy adjustments, and renewable energy maximization.

Mean Optimization Reward by Time Slot & Location

Figure 6.1: Mean optimization reward across time slots and location types. Positive values indicate favorable grid conditions; negative values indicate suboptimal states.

Actionable Recommendations

R1: Implement Queue-Aware Dynamic Scheduling

Deploy predictive queue management at the top 10 high-wait stations. Shift non-urgent (Low priority) sessions to adjacent time windows using real-time queue-length triggers. This directly addresses the r=-0.01 queue-wait correlation.

Target: Reduce P90 wait by 25%

R2: Introduce Renewable-Responsive Pricing

The current price-renewable correlation is only r=-0.005. Implement a dynamic tariff that discounts electricity during high-renewable windows (Clear weather, Off-Peak) to shift demand toward greener periods and improve the optimization reward.

Target: Improve renewable ratio during Peak by 10–15%

R3: Load-Shift Highway Peak Demand to Off-Peak

Highway stations during Peak slots average 84.0 kW load. Introduce Off-Peak charging incentives (discounted rates, priority lane access) to smooth the load curve and reduce grid stress during critical windows.

Target: 15–20% Peak load reduction at Highway stations

R4: Prioritize High-Capacity Vehicle Charging Off-Peak

Buses and Trucks consume 39–39 kWh per session. Designate Off-Peak charging windows for fleet operators with guaranteed capacity, reducing Peak grid load while offering cost savings.

Target: Shift 30% of heavy-vehicle sessions to Off-Peak

R5: Expand Capacity at High-Demand Stations

Station ST012 leads in demand (56.1) with elevated wait times. Add charger units and consider transformer upgrades at the top 5 highest-demand stations to relieve bottlenecks.

Target: Reduce avg wait at top 5 stations by 30%

R6: Weather-Aware Charging Incentives

Renewable ratio peaks at 35.7% during Clear weather. Send real-time notifications to app users when renewable availability is high, offering small per-kWh discounts to nudge session timing toward greener windows.

Target: +5% renewable utilization during non-Clear weather

Synthesis

▸The dataset reveals a clear tension between customer experience (wait times) and grid optimization (load balancing). Highway stations during Peak hours are the critical pressure point, with average waits of 9.6 minutes and loads of 84.0 kW.
▸The optimization reward metric (mean: -11.83) provides a useful composite signal. Positive rewards are most achievable during Off-Peak Clear-weather sessions — aligning interventions with these conditions will yield the best grid-level outcomes.
▸Recommendations R2 and R6 can be implemented quickly with software-only changes and offer the best ROI in the near term. R1 and R3 require operational process changes. R5 involves capital expenditure but addresses structural bottlenecks.
